context_requirements: Intact ROCK1/ROCK2 expression and RhoA-ROCK signaling
Adherent, substrate-attached cells with active actomyosin contractility
Responsiveness is largely cytoprotective and anti-apoptotic rather than a strong transcriptional program
falsifiers: No reproducible directional change in any landmark gene at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine lines
Strong, uniform upregulation of proliferation and cell-cycle genes at 24 h across all lines
A response pattern indistinguishable from generic stress or DNA-damage signatures without any ROCK-pathway-linked genes

evidence.supports: ROCK inhibition promotes corneal endothelial cell adhesion, proliferation and survival
ROCK inhibitor offsets TGFbeta2-induced ECM and fibrotic gene expression changes
Y-27632 suppresses IL-1beta/TGF-beta receptor and caspase-8/-10 apoptotic pathway genes
Y-27632 protects human cardiac stem cells from doxorubicin-induced apoptosis
Y-27632 reduces dissociation-induced apoptosis and improves survival of primate ES cells

changes: Moved RHOA from proximal_up to proximal_down: ROCK inhibition reduces RhoA-ROCK signaling and downstream contractility, so RHOA pathway output should decrease, not increase.
Moved MYL9 from proximal_up to proximal_down: MYL9 (myosin light chain) phosphorylation/contractility is directly inhibited by ROCK inhibition.
Moved TJP1 from proximal_up to proximal_down: tight junction assembly is disrupted by loss of ROCK-dependent actomyosin tension.
Moved CD44 from proximal_up to proximal_down: CD44 is a contractility-associated adhesion receptor whose expression is reduced by ROCK inhibition.
Moved SERPINE1 from proximal_up to proximal_down: ROCK inhibition reduces TGFbeta/ECM-driven SERPINE1 expression.
Moved IL1B from late_up to late_down: Y-27632 suppresses IL-1beta pathway genes (PMID 22133891).
Moved CXCL2 from late_up to late_down: inflammatory chemokine expression is suppressed by ROCK inhibition.
Moved COL1A1 from late_up to late_down: ROCK inhibition has anti-fibrotic activity and reduces collagen expression (PMID 27924833).
Moved COL4A1 from late_up to late_down: ECM/collagen genes are reduced by ROCK inhibition (PMID 27924833).
Moved TIMP2 from late_up to late_down: TIMP2 is part of the ECM/fibrotic program reduced by ROCK inhibition.
Moved MMP2 from late_up to late_down: MMP2 is an ECM-remodeling gene reduced by ROCK inhibition.
Moved TGFB3 from late_up to late_down: TGFbeta signaling is suppressed by ROCK inhibition (PMID 22133891, PMID 27924833).
Removed CCND1 from proximal_up: CCND1 is a generic proliferation gene, not a proximal ROCK target.
Removed MYC from proximal_up: MYC is a generic proliferation gene, not a proximal ROCK target.
Removed CDKN1A from late_up: CDKN1A is a generic stress/cell-cycle arrest gene.
Removed CDKN1B from late_up: CDKN1B is a generic cell-cycle gene.
Removed GADD45A from late_up: GADD45A is a generic stress/DNA-damage gene.
Removed CCNB1, CDK1, AURKB, BIRC5, TOP2A, UBE2C, PLK1, KIF20A, NUSAP1, STMN1 from proximal_down: these are generic proliferation/cell-cycle genes, not proximal ROCK targets.
Removed CCNA2, CCNE2, E2F2, MCM3, PCNA, RFC2, RFC5, CHEK1, MYBL2, KIF14 from late_down: these are generic proliferation/cell-cycle genes, not specific late ROCK targets.
Changed kinetics from slow to fast: ROCK inhibition affects actomyosin contractility and immediate-early genes within minutes to hours, so 6 h should show clear changes.
Changed magnitude 6h from weak to moderate: direct ROCK inhibition produces measurable early transcriptional changes.
Changed magnitude 24h from moderate to weak: the response is largely cytoprotective/anti-apoptotic rather than a strong sustained transcriptional program.
Changed line_response for all lines from weak to moderate: ROCK1/ROCK2 are broadly expressed and ROCK inhibition affects adherent cells across lineages.
Removed PMID 26645568 from evidence: abstract describes protection from doxorubicin-induced apoptosis, not a transcriptional response to ROCK inhibition alone.
Removed PMID 18940855 from evidence: abstract describes improved survival and colony formation, not transcriptional profiling.
